root/code-structure-converse/code-induce.summary: Every deterministic finite-block private-message code induces variables satisfying the exact fixed-map factorization, four rate rows, and an absolute dependence-balance defect bounded by max(delta_1,delta_2). This is a sequence-level necessary condition, not by itself a fixed-cardinality single-letter outer region.
root/code-structure-converse/code-induce.title: Code-induced finite-block dependence balance

root/code-structure-converse/copy-extens.summary: Because the counterfeit is an actual finite distribution, every universally valid finite-variable information inequality holds at it. Standard finite copy-lemma extensions can be realized by conditional resampling while preserving the original marginal and objective, so they cannot remove the witness.
root/code-structure-converse/copy-extens.title: Finite copy-extension obstruction

root/code-structure-converse/entropy-cop.summary: For the specified coarse entropy relaxation, an entropic feasible point attains 2h_2(1/4)-5/4 on both direct branches. Consequently, universally valid finite-variable information inequalities and finite standard copy-lemma sequences cannot lower that relaxation below this value. The obstruction does not cover exact binary-posterior or other channel-specific consistency constraints.
root/code-structure-converse/entropy-cop.title: Entropy and copy-lemma refinement no-go

root/code-structure-converse/entropy-cou.summary: An explicit distribution built from independent binary components satisfies the stated coarse BSSC entropy vector, structural equalities, dependence balance, all specified conditional BEC identities, and both sharp support rows. Both direct sum branches equal 2h_2(1/4)-5/4.
root/code-structure-converse/entropy-cou.title: Explicit finite entropic counterfeit witness

root/code-structure-converse/exact-witne.summary: A standard-library symbolic checker represents every component entropy as an affine expression in h_2(1/4) and verifies component positivity, the base entropy vector, structural equalities, dependence balance, all 65 disjoint-subtuple BEC identities, both support rows, and both objective branches without floating-point arithmetic.
root/code-structure-converse/exact-witne.title: Exact affine entropy witness checker

root/code-structure-converse/finite-bloc.summary: The proof introduces S_i=(Y^{i-1},Z_{i+1}^n), telescopes the conditional message-dependence difference to the two block-output endpoints, and applies separate Fano bounds. Time sampling preserves message and time independence, the fixed encoder map, the memoryless law, and four compatible rate inequalities.
root/code-structure-converse/finite-bloc.title: Finite-block dependence-balance telescope

root/multiletter-marton-achievability/tw.summary: Assuming the Geng--Jog--Nair--Wang binary-input Marton theorem, every finite Marton law for the half-skew BSSC product channel whose induced super-input is supported on at most two of the four symbols has sum-rate strictly below 0.615 bit. Since product randomized time division exceeds 0.7232857688439092 bits, any strict two-letter Marton improvement over the current BSSC achievable rate must use at least three super-input symbols. The result does not exclude gains on three- or four-symbol support.
root/multiletter-marton-achievability/tw.title: Two-letter Marton two-symbol support pruning

root/multiletter-marton-achievability/tw.summary: A Python standard-library checker constructs the product receiver marginals with exact rational arithmetic, verifies the six-support orbit classification and the adjacent, antirepetition, and repetition transition structures, and uses directed high-precision Decimal intervals to check the repetition-support tangent bound, the strict 0.615-bit endpoint, and its separation from 0.7232857688439092 bits.
root/multiletter-marton-achievability/tw.title: Exact two-symbol orbit and tangent-certificate verifier

root/multiletter-marton-achievability/tw.summary: The six unordered two-symbol supports in {00,01,10,11} reduce to four adjacent supports and two diagonal supports. The diagonal supports split into the antirepetition pair {01,10} and the repetition pair {00,11}; singleton supports convey no information. This exhausts all super-input supports of size at most two.
root/multiletter-marton-achievability/tw.title: Two-symbol super-input orbit reduction

root/multiletter-marton-achievability/tw.summary: Adjacent supports discard an input-independent product coordinate and admit a cooperative binary-erasure upper bound of 1/2 bit; the antirepetition support likewise has binary-erasure receiver marginals and a 1/2-bit cooperative bound. For the repetition support, the assumed binary-input Marton theorem reduces the sum-rate to randomized time division. Concavity and reflection symmetry of its receiver-information curve, together with a tangent bound on the receiver-information difference, give a strict upper bound below 0.615 bit.
root/multiletter-marton-achievability/tw.title: Rate bounds for the two-symbol support classes

root/theorem9-auxiliary-receiver-convers.summary: A common-mixture coupling of the joint input-output laws at two binary input priors bounds both the input entropy change and the conditional input entropy change by h_2(|p-p'|). Subtraction yields |J_A(p)-J_A(p')|≤2h_2(|p-p'|), uniformly over the receiver output alphabet and also for generalized posterior-measure receivers.
root/theorem9-auxiliary-receiver-convers.title: Alphabet-free uniform continuity of binary receiver curves

root/theorem9-auxiliary-receiver-convers.summary: A dependency-free standard-library checker validates the two declared dependency transactions, independently rebuilds the accepted generic length-three 30-row system, combines identical signed atoms, checks every audited (a_r,b_r) coefficient and the global (4,4) bound, and verifies the support, reflection, and mesh formulas for the explicit uniform grids. It does not mechanically prove the entropy-continuity, Carathéodory, or compactness arguments.
root/theorem9-auxiliary-receiver-convers.title: Deterministic receiver-curve stability verifier

root/theorem9-auxiliary-receiver-convers.summary: A dependency-free standard-library verifier checks the encoded factorization, all sixteen cited equation labels, both side conditions, exact agreement between the expanded and independently generated 30-row systems, and the exhaustive single-output term whitelist used for product-marginal reduction. It makes no PDF-origin, rendering, source-fidelity, or visual-semantic assertion.
root/theorem9-auxiliary-receiver-convers.title: Exact Theorem 9 specialization auditor

root/theorem9-auxiliary-receiver-convers.summary: A dependency-free standard-library Python verifier reconstructs the accepted 30-row path system, checks its normalized signature and receiver-skew symmetry, and verifies all row and block-box slacks for the three Q0 witness families using exact rational-polynomial arithmetic. It also checks the matching common-curve upper row. The verifier uses no floating-point optimization and explicitly does not re-prove the external Carathéodory theorem or authenticate the dependency transaction.
root/theorem9-auxiliary-receiver-convers.title: Exact finite-grid Q0 witness verifier

root/theorem9-auxiliary-receiver-convers.summary: Represent a finite-output binary-input receiver at the fair prior by its finite posterior measure of mean 1/2, expressing every sampled receiver-information value as an integral of a scalar posterior function. Applying the finite-dimensional Carathéodory theorem to the posterior coordinate and the nonendpoint samples on an N-point grid gives an at-most-N-atom measure preserving every sample on the grid. The receiver-information identities for the accepted 30-row system then preserve the complete restricted optimization. For reflection-closed grids, applying the reduction to one posterior measure and reflecting it preserves the reflected receiver class. This argument is only for fixed finite grids and does not furnish a continuum cardinality bound.
root/theorem9-auxiliary-receiver-convers.title: Posterior-measure proof of the finite-grid receiver reduction

root/theorem9-auxiliary-receiver-convers.summary: For every N-point posterior grid Q containing 0, 1/2, and 1, each finite-output binary-input receiver has an at-most-N-output replacement with identical mutual-information samples on Q. Consequently the unrestricted finite-receiver infimum of V_Q equals the infimum over receiver pairs with at most N outputs each. If Q is reflection closed, the analogous reflected-pair infimum equals the infimum over posterior measures with support size at most N. No continuum cardinality, attainment, or limit-interchange conclusion is asserted.
root/theorem9-auxiliary-receiver-convers.title: Finite-grid auxiliary-receiver cardinality reduction

root/theorem9-auxiliary-receiver-convers.summary: Assuming the cited Theorem 9 outer-bound premise exactly as encoded by the declared dependency, the fixed binary auxiliary receivers with output-zero probabilities 0.206961624915382 and 0.826953249115544 for G and 0.173046750884456 and 0.793038375084618 for K yield C_sum ≤ U, where U lies in [0.36929694596920284244271335135600317726937686320586339865039784778686683932875798, 0.36929694596920284244271335135600317726937686320586339865039784778686683932875818]. Hence C_sum ≤ 0.369296945969202842443. This fixed-pair certificate neither authenticates the cited premise nor asserts receiver or dual optimality, a matching achievable rate, or the exact sum capacity.
root/theorem9-auxiliary-receiver-convers.title: Premise-bounded BSSC upper bound from an attested fixed receiver pair

root/theorem9-auxiliary-receiver-convers.summary: A Python standard-library verifier checks the receiver reflection identities, exact six-row weights and combined tensor, continuous inner and outer inequalities using directed Decimal intervals, the all-priors reduction, hostile ambient Decimal contexts, the claimed final interval, and the rounded headline bound. It fails on unresolved interval cells, evidence drift, or any failed assertion.
root/theorem9-auxiliary-receiver-convers.title: Exact fixed-pair dual-certificate verifier

root/theorem9-auxiliary-receiver-convers.summary: Affine inner majorants and affine outer majorants bound the three reduced posterior groups over the complete interval [0,1]. Exact curvature, ordering, tangent, endpoint, reflection, and directed-interval subdivision arguments establish the inequalities continuously rather than on a sampled grid. The resulting prior bound is concave and reflection symmetric, so its global maximum occurs at the fair prior, yielding the certified narrow interval for U without invoking strong duality, minimax exchange, or receiver optimality.
root/theorem9-auxiliary-receiver-convers.title: Continuous weak-duality certificate for the fixed receiver pair

root/theorem9-auxiliary-receiver-convers.summary: For the specified exact-decimal binary auxiliary receivers, a nonnegative exact-rational combination of six premise-bound private-message rows gives unit coefficients on both private rates. Expanding the information terms into posterior information functions and applying the common-mean and martingale identities reduces the resulting bound to three scalar posterior groups and an affine prior term.
root/theorem9-auxiliary-receiver-convers.title: Six-row posterior weak-duality reduction for the fixed receiver pair

root/theorem9-auxiliary-receiver-convers.summary: Mean-one-half Borel posterior measures form a weakly compact space. Pointwise continuity of the posterior information integrand, together with the common binary-prior continuity modulus, upgrades weak convergence to uniform convergence of receiver curves. Carathéodory matching on any N-point grid containing 0, 1/2, and 1, followed by the common modulus, gives an at-most-N-output exact grid match with sup-norm error at most min{1,4h_2(Delta_Q)}. Reflection of the reduced measure preserves an already reflected pair on reflection-closed grids.
root/theorem9-auxiliary-receiver-convers.title: Compact generalized receiver curves and uniform finite-output density

root/theorem9-auxiliary-receiver-convers.summary: An exhaustive audit of every output-bearing information term shows that replacing an arbitrary admitted joint auxiliary-receiver law by the product of its input-only G and K marginals preserves all 30 specialized rows and both directions of feasibility. Input-only product receiver pairs are therefore sufficient for the resulting infimum bound.
root/theorem9-auxiliary-receiver-convers.title: Input-only product-marginal receiver reduction

root/theorem9-auxiliary-receiver-convers.summary: Conditional on the encoded cited Theorem 9 outer-bound premise, the physical BSSC private-message sum capacity satisfies C_sum ≤ inf B(G,K), where the infimum ranges over finite-output binary-input input-only receiver channels T_{G|X} and T_{K|X}, with B defined by first optimizing the specialized finite auxiliary hierarchy at fixed input prior and receivers and then taking the supremum over the prior.
root/theorem9-auxiliary-receiver-convers.title: Premise-bounded auxiliary-receiver sum-capacity converse

root/theorem9-auxiliary-receiver-convers.summary: With the explicit extended-real convention sup(empty set)=-∞, every finite posterior-support restriction Q containing 1/2 satisfies V_Q(G,K) ≤ V(1/2;G,K) ≤ B(G,K). For Q0={0,1/2,1}, all specialized rows depend on the receiver channels only through their midpoint information values (c,g,k,c), so V_0(g,k) is unambiguous and finite on the realizable (g,k)-domain.
root/theorem9-auxiliary-receiver-convers.title: Finite-support local auxiliary-receiver values

root/theorem9-auxiliary-receiver-convers.summary: For Q0={0,1/2,1} and c=h_2(1/4)-1/2, both the unrestricted finite-receiver infimum and the reflected finite-receiver infimum of V_Q0 equal c. For every finite-output input-only receiver pair, with g=J_G(1/2) and k=J_K(1/2), B(G,K)≥V_0(g,k)≥max{F(g),F(k)} for F(x)=2c max{c,x}/(c+x). Hence c≤U<2c and B(G,K)≤U force 2c^2/U-c≤g,k≤Uc/(2c-U). These conclusions are confined to the finite Q0 rung and necessary coercivity; they do not assert a continuum limit, a limit interchange, or full-functional reflected optimality.
root/theorem9-auxiliary-receiver-convers.title: Exact Q0 receiver infima and coercive midpoint window

root/theorem9-auxiliary-receiver-convers.summary: The reflection-invariant posterior measure placing mass c/2 at each endpoint and mass 1-c at the midpoint defines a three-output revealing-erasure receiver with sampled information curve (0,c,0) on Q0. Substitution into the accepted specialized rows gives a feasible reflected receiver pair with local value at most c, matching the universal Q0 lower bound. This is a finite-grid construction and does not establish reflected optimality for the full functional B.
root/theorem9-auxiliary-receiver-convers.title: Matching three-output reflected receiver on Q0

root/theorem9-auxiliary-receiver-convers.summary: On Q0={0,1/2,1}, parameterize each auxiliary hierarchy block by its endpoint and midpoint posterior masses. Three explicit feasible witness families covering the cases where the two midpoint receiver values are above, below, or on opposite sides of c=h_2(1/4)-1/2 establish V_0(g,k) at least max{F(g),F(k)}, where F(x)=2c max{c,x}/(c+x). Combining this with the accepted inequality B(G,K)≥V_0(g,k), and inverting the two branches of F, proves that c≤U<2c and B(G,K)≤U imply 2c^2/U-c≤g,k≤Uc/(2c-U). The window is necessary only.
root/theorem9-auxiliary-receiver-convers.title: Q0 primal witnesses and midpoint coercivity

root/theorem9-auxiliary-receiver-convers.summary: Setting R0=0 in the encoded premise, expanding every displayed minimum, and splitting both interval side conditions produces 26 private-rate and nonnegativity rows plus four side-condition rows. Exact normalization shows that these 30 rows coincide term by term with the independently generated local length-three path system.
root/theorem9-auxiliary-receiver-convers.title: Exact R0=0 thirty-row specialization

root/theorem9-auxiliary-receiver-convers.summary: For a fixed auxiliary hierarchy, replacing G and K by uniformly close receiver curves preserves feasibility after relaxing row r by a_r epsilon_G+b_r epsilon_K; the reverse comparison follows by exchanging the receiver pairs. If every original row has slack exceeding its corresponding perturbation allowance, the same rates and hierarchy remain feasible, so strictly feasible witnesses persist under sufficiently fine finite-output approximations. The argument does not establish convergence of the unrelaxed optimized functional when rate-free constraints are active with zero margin.
root/theorem9-auxiliary-receiver-convers.title: Relaxed-row stability and strict-feasibility persistence

root/theorem9-auxiliary-receiver-convers.summary: Combining identical signed receiver-information atoms in each accepted specialized row and applying the exact term sensitivities produces the audited rowwise coefficient pairs (a_r,b_r). Every pair is coordinatewise at most (4,4), so sup-norm receiver-curve perturbations epsilon_G and epsilon_K alter each row right side by at most a_r epsilon_G+b_r epsilon_K and universally by at most 4epsilon_G+4epsilon_K.
root/theorem9-auxiliary-receiver-convers.title: Exact 30-row receiver-curve sensitivity audit

root/theorem9-auxiliary-receiver-convers.summary: Every binary-input receiver curve satisfies |J_A(p)-J_A(p')|≤2h_2(|p-p'|). Generalized mean-one-half posterior-measure receiver curves form a compact subset of C([0,1]) with uniformly dense finite-output curves; on every N-point grid Q containing 0, 1/2, and 1, an at-most-N-output exact grid match has sup-norm error at most min{1,4h_2(Delta_Q)}, while reflection-closed grids preserve an already reflected pair. For the accepted 30-row system, receiver errors epsilon_G and epsilon_K require only the audited row relaxations a_r epsilon_G+b_r epsilon_K, bounded universally by 4epsilon_G+4epsilon_K, and strictly feasible witnesses persist under sufficiently fine approximation. No unrelaxed optimized-value convergence, full-functional cardinality bound, reflected optimality, minimax interchange, numerical capacity improvement, or exact sum-capacity conclusion follows.
root/theorem9-auxiliary-receiver-convers.title: Uniform receiver-curve continuum bridge and 30-row stability

root/uv-scalar-converse/averaged-uv-prod.summary: For arbitrary finite-alphabet discrete memoryless broadcast channels, the averaged scalar B_avg defined from the two separately relaxed UV rows satisfies B_avg(W1×W2)=B_avg(W1)+B_avg(W2). The theorem includes correlated product-channel priors and envelope auxiliaries joint across factors, but does not tensorize the complete UV region.
root/uv-scalar-converse/averaged-uv-prod.title: Exact additivity of the averaged UV scalar

root/uv-scalar-converse/bssc-uv-blocking.summary: For every finite n≥1, the half-skew BSSC P satisfies B_br(P^×n)=B_avg(P^×n)=n(2h_2(1/4)-5/4), with normalized value 0.3725562489182657… bits per channel use. This valid UV converse is weaker than the certified full-Theorem-9 upper bound 0.369296945969202842443 and therefore changes neither endpoint of the governed capacity interval.
root/uv-scalar-converse/bssc-uv-blocking.title: All-blocklength branchwise UV value for the half-skew BSSC

root/uv-scalar-converse/bssc-uv-envelope.summary: Using the sharp BSSC posterior support represented by the dependency transaction, the fair invariant prior and an exact posterior contact decomposition evaluate the one-letter scalar as 2h_2(1/4)-5/4.
root/uv-scalar-converse/bssc-uv-envelope.title: Exact half-skew BSSC UV envelope contact

root/uv-scalar-converse/correlated-input.summary: A conditional chain-rule identity cancels the cross-factor correction terms for the receiver-information difference. Conditioning leaves valid one-factor auxiliaries, yielding upper-concave-envelope subadditivity even when the product input is correlated and the envelope auxiliary is joint across factors; product priors and product posterior decompositions provide the reverse inequality.
root/uv-scalar-converse/correlated-input.title: Correlated-input envelope factorization

root/uv-scalar-converse/half-skew-bssc-c.summary: At the invariant binary input prior, the half-skew BSSC receiver informations equal h_2(1/4)-1/2. The sharp posterior-support inequality and the posterior mixture with masses 5/8 at q=4/5 and 3/8 at q=0 give envelope value h_2(1/4)-3/4, yielding the one-letter scalar 2h_2(1/4)-5/4 bits.
root/uv-scalar-converse/half-skew-bssc-c.title: Half-skew BSSC posterior-contact evaluation

root/uv-scalar-converse/half-skew-bssc-s.summary: A standard-library high-precision script checks the half-skew channel relabeling identities, the attaining posterior mixture, the support-contact equality, and the numerical value of 2h_2(1/4)-5/4. It corroborates the exact specialization but does not replace the analytic product and symmetry proof.
root/uv-scalar-converse/half-skew-bssc-s.title: High-precision half-skew BSSC specialization audit

root/uv-scalar-converse/product-envelope.summary: A conditional Csiszár sum identity factors the receiver-information difference across product-channel coordinates, including correlated input laws and joint envelope auxiliaries. Product posterior ensembles give the reverse inequality. An involutive receiver-exchanging input relabeling then identifies the two relaxed rows at invariant priors and extends the equality to finite receiver-skew products.
root/uv-scalar-converse/product-envelope.title: Product-envelope factorization and receiver-skew reduction

root/uv-scalar-converse/receiver-skew-br.summary: For a finite-alphabet receiver-skew-symmetric broadcast channel, B_br equals B_avg and an optimum can be sought among invariant input laws. Finite products preserve the symmetry, so both scalars are exactly additive on arbitrary finite products of channels in this class. No equality is asserted for nonsymmetric channels or for a common joint UV optimization.
root/uv-scalar-converse/receiver-skew-br.title: Branchwise UV additivity under receiver-skew symmetry

root/uv-scalar-converse/receiver-skew-in.summary: An involutive input relabeling that exchanges the receivers maps the information difference t to -t and swaps the two relaxed rows A and D. Concavity at the symmetrized input law shows that the branchwise minimum reaches the averaged value and permits restriction to invariant input laws.
root/uv-scalar-converse/receiver-skew-in.title: Receiver-skew invariant-prior reduction

root/uv-scalar-converse/separately-relax.summary: For finite-alphabet discrete memoryless broadcast channels, the averaged separately relaxed UV sum-rate scalar is exactly additive under products. For receiver-skew channels the branchwise scalar equals the averaged scalar, and both are additive on every finite receiver-skew product. Hence, for the half-skew BSSC P and every n≥1, both scalars on P^×n equal n(2h_2(1/4)-5/4) bits. This does not assert tensorization of the full UV region, a common joint-(U,V) optimization, the GK functional, or capacity.
root/uv-scalar-converse/separately-relax.title: Tensorization theorem for separately relaxed UV scalars

root/uv-scalar-converse/uv-factorization.summary: Dependency-free executable checks corroborate the conditional chain identities, mutual-information subadditivity, product posterior mixtures, receiver-skew identities, deterministic and zero-probability edge cases, and high-precision BSSC contact evaluation. These checks support but do not replace the analytic finite-alphabet proofs.
